validity.recommendation: Keep the row (real, well-sourced pipeline) but review tracker placement: this is an ETHANE feedstock line, not a methane sales-gas trunk. Human should decide whether it belongs in GGIT (gas) or GOIT/NGL. Add the MEED refs staged below.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE — CONFIRMED. Two MEED trade-press articles name this exact line. (1) 'Aramco tenders major pipeline jobs' (meed.com/aramco-tenders-major-pipeline-jobs): 'a 38-inch, 56-kilometre ethane line looped with two existing pipelines and aimed at transporting 820 million cubic feet a day of gas to Jubail industrial city ... between the Juaymah gas plant and Jubail'; scope also included a right-of-way road and removal of two existing pipeline sections. (2) 'CAT pounces on pipelines' (meed.com/cat-pounces-on-pipelines, the sheet's existing Capacity/Length ref): '38-inch-diameter, 56-kilometre-long ethane line ... 820 million cubic feet a day of gas to Jubail industrial city', SR103m ($27.5m) two-year EPC awarded to Lebanon's Contracting & Trading Co (CAT), client Saudi Aramco. Specs (56 km, 820 MMcf/d, 38 in, Juaymah->Jubail, Aramco) match the GEM row precisely. NOTE: the gem.wiki page's only outbound citations are two OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin pages (ASB2012 p.75, ASB2013 p.79) which do NOT name this pipeline — wiki support alone is existence-weak; the MEED sourcing is what carries it. CLASSIFICATION — this is an ETHANE line feeding Jubail Industrial City petrochemical crackers (ethane is an NGL component, though gaseous and measured here in MMcf/d). GEM lists Fuel=Gas; defensible but genuinely borderline vs an NGL/petrochemical-feedstock line. Flagging for a human GGIT-vs-GOIT scope call. DUPLICATE — checked against the full 40-row SA gas operating roster and the 20-feature GulfPub SA gas roster: no counterpart. Nearest names (P1901 UBTG-1km-Juaymah 204 km, P1902 Safaniyah-Ju'aymah 198 km) are different lines by length/route; GulfPub has no Juaymah->Jubail feature. Not a duplicate. ATTRIBUTION — Owner/operator Saudi Aramco (client on both MEED contracts) is correct; FuelSource 'Al Juaima'h' (Ju'aymah gas fractionation plant) is correct.

Capacity 820 MMcf/d: CONFIRMED by both ('820 million cubic feet a day'); note this is the throughput of the looped system, not of the 38-in line alone. Diameter: MEED sources only the NEW '38-inch' line and says it is 'looped with two existing pipelines'; the GEM multi-value '38,30, 40' likely lumps the two existing looped lines (30 in, 40 in) with the new 38-in line — plausible but 30/40 are NOT independently sourced here. Status 'operating': the only sources are construction-era EPC tender/award reports (~mid-2000s, Hawiyah NGL recovery era); no independent source explicitly confirms current operating status, though a mid-2000s-built Aramco feeder is very likely operating. Treating operating as presumed, ref UNRESOLVED.

routes.start_name: Ju'aymah gas (fractionation) plant, near Ras Tanura, Eastern Province
routes.corridor_desc: Runs roughly northwest along the Persian Gulf coastal strip of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, from the Ju'aymah gas fractionation complex near Ras Tanura to Jubail Industrial City, ~56 km. MEED describes the 38-in line as 'looped with two existing pipelines', so the corridor follows an established multi-line right-of-way between the two facilities. Endpoints are named and well-located; the exact intermediate alignment is not published, so the corridor is bounded to the coastal Ju'aymah->Jubail band rather than a precise trace.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from MEED ('between the Juaymah gas plant and Jubail'). Coordinates are approximate but defensible from the well-known locations of the Ju'aymah/Ras Tanura complex (~26.88N, 49.92E) and Jubail Industrial City (~27.0N, 49.66E); no coordinates were fabricated for the intermediate route, which is left as a coastal corridor. Length ~56 km is consistent with the ~50-60 km coastal separation of the two sites.

summary: P1909 Juaymah-Jubail exists (2 MEED articles, exact spec match) but is an ETHANE feedstock line, not methane sales gas — classification caveat; diameter 30/40 in unsourced (38 only); status 'operating' presumed, ref UNRESOLVED.
